findings.finding: Revenue = cloud consumption and seat subscriptions on a fixed, fast-growing datacenter base. Azure is the growth engine: Azure revenue +48% y/y in Q1 FY2027 (33.2B of 92.3B total), Microsoft Cloud 63.9B +30%; Q2 FY2027 Azure guided +49-50% cc. Agents and Infra segment +24.5% while Devices and Consumer -3.2% (Windows OEM and Devices -22%).

Group growth +18.8% y/y in Q1 FY2027 and +18.8% implied by the Q2 guide midpoint (96.55B vs 81.27B). Structural part: Azure/AI consumption and M365 commercial (+17%); cyclical part: PC/Windows OEM (-22%) and Xbox content (-2%) are shrinking; the econ review could not split units x price (customers missing), so the split is qualitative with a residual.

OpenAI is a related party and 10.8% of Q1 revenue (10.0B), with a 7.2B receivable, a 24% as-converted stake and 12.0B of a 13.0B funding commitment already funded: MSFT partly finances a large customer. No other customer above 10%. OpenAI's share of the 677B commercial RPO is not disclosed.

Commercial RPO 677B (+73% y/y), weighted duration 2.3 years, about 30% (about 203B) recognized in the next 12 months: contracted demand covers more than half of the next year's revenue. Sequentially flat vs 678B at Q4 FY2026, so bookings slowed in the quarter.

Cash capex 39.4B in Q1 FY2027 (+103% y/y), 45.2B including finance leases, guided above 50B in Q2 and rising in H2; about three quarters on short-lived servers/GPUs. FY2026 capex 115.9B vs 64.6B in FY2025. Datacenter leases not yet commenced 364.6B and purchase commitments 194.1B (169.0B within a year) make a large fixed cost base if demand slows. FCF margin fell from 33% (FY2021) to 20% (FY2026 and Q1 FY2027).

Operating margin 49.8% in Q1 FY2027 vs 41.6-46.8% in FY2021-FY2026 (quarter review flag peak_margin_run_rate): opex grew 6% vs revenue 19%. Gross margin fell 125 bp y/y as depreciation of the AI fleet rises (D&A 34.3B in FY2026 vs 22.0B FY2025). Q2 guide (revenue 96.55B, COGS 32.8B, opex 18.55B) implies about 46.8% operating margin. Normalized Q1 EPS 4.89 vs reported 4.92 (OpenAI gain 207M after tax removed); FY2026 EPS 17.95 includes OpenAI gains, FY2025 losses.

Microsoft guides one quarter at a time, only on the call; there is no fiscal-year revenue guidance and auto.json has no track-record ratio. One checkable point: Q1 FY2027 revenue guided 89.85-90.95B, actual 92.28B (about 2% above the midpoint 90.4B), Azure guided ~45% cc, actual 48%: a conservative guider on this one observation, so the Q2 guide reads as a floor, not a ceiling.

Piotroski 6/9 (mixed), Altman Z'' 4.59 (safe), Beneish unavailable; ROIC 31% last, 34% average, incremental ROIC 23.6% and falling as capital floods in (still well above an 8% reference). SBC 12.4B = 3.7% of FY2026 revenue (4.4% FY2024), buybacks 22.3B exceed SBC; diluted shares 7,446M vs 7,466M a year ago (-0.3%).

Cash and short-term investments 64.5B vs debt 35.5B (net cash 29.0B), but finance lease liabilities of 71.0B at 2026-09-30 sit outside the debt lines and are a debt-like claim; operating leases are an operating cost. Company says it stays FCF positive in FY2027 and may use outside financing (call, secondary).

Computed mature_growth / stalwart confirmed by the revenue size (331.8B FY2026) and 15% revenue CAGR FY2021-FY2026, but growth has re-accelerated to ~19% with Azure at ~48%: a large compounder in an AI capacity build. The lens is reinvestment returns (incremental ROIC vs capex) and backlog conversion, not a cheap-multiple screen.

flags: peak_margin_run_rate (high): Q1 FY2027 operating margin 49.8% vs historical median 44.6%; a quarter x 4 is a peak run rate, carried to the bear (margin falls back as depreciation of short-lived AI assets ramps)
weak_cash_conversion (medium): Q1 FCF 18.6B = 51% of normalized net income; capex 68% of operating cash flow; carried to the bear and the key risk
segment_shrinking (medium): Devices and Consumer -3.2% y/y, Windows OEM and Devices -22%; carried to the bear
customer concentration: OpenAI 10.8% of revenue, a related party partly funded by MSFT (12.0B funded) with a 7.2B receivable; carried to the key risk
fixed-cost overhang: 364.6B of datacenter leases not yet commenced and 169.0B of purchase commitments due within a year; carried to the bear
incremental ROIC 23.6% below the 34% average: returns on new capital are falling; carried to the bear
acquisition flag FY2024 (Activision): part of FY2024 growth was bought, the type uses growth without that year
Beneish M-score unavailable (inputs missing): a visible gap, not a pass

economics.reason: Revenue grew every year FY2021-FY2026 (7%-18%), operating margin moved only 41.6%-46.8% (volatility 2.0 points), and recurring cloud/subscription revenue is backed by a 677B commercial RPO; the AI capex cycle is a capacity build with an overbuild risk, carried to the bear, not an industry price cycle in revenue.

gaps: no fiscal-year revenue guidance and no multi-quarter guidance track record (one observation, Q1 FY2027); the Q1 call was read through a secondary summary only
OpenAI share of the 677B commercial RPO not disclosed
consensus (Alpha Vantage, dated 2026-11-01) not citable until 2026-11-03: not used as a driver or cross-check
Beneish inputs missing; recast FY2026 history for the new segment structure not available
Copilot seats / AI revenue run rate not disclosed as levels
